title: Signs of hypertension detected by a smartwatch
summary: Prospective study of 196 people at five US sites, compared with 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure measurement: 65.8% sensitivity and 90.0% specificity for screening, and 78.4% and 90.9% in the confirmatory test (48 participants). A feasibility study; it does not replace the cuff, and many cases are missed.

evidence.tested: A prospective study of 196 participants at five US sites compared smartwatch screening with 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring: 65.8% sensitivity and 90.0% specificity, with 78.4% and 90.9% in a confirmatory subgroup of 48.
evidence.unknown: The authors call it early feasibility research; the smartwatch does not replace a cuff, many true cases are missed, the confirmatory subgroup is small, and generalizability is unclear.
evidence.ai_role: A 1-D convolutional network pretrained with self-supervised contrastive learning on PPG and accelerometer waveforms produced embeddings; a logistic regression output a hypertension probability.
